bug_description.original: A heap-use-after-free exists in xinclude.c: xmlXIncludeCopyXPointer reads memory that has already been freed during XInclude processing (called via xmlXIncludeIncludeNode/xmlXIncludeDoProcess). Malicious or malformed XInclude/XPointer input can trigger this read-after-free, leading to crashes or memory corruption and potential exploitation.
bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` uses libxml2's fuzz-XML envelope: its first four bytes decode to `0x2020ffff`, which sets both `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` and `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE`, and its remaining bytes provide the main entity later parsed by `xmlReadMemory()`. Because the XInclude bit is set, the parsed document enters `xmlXIncludeProcessFlags(doc, opts)`, and `xmlXIncludeSetFlags()` stores that attacker-controlled option word in `ctxt->parseFlags`. During XInclude collection, accepted include nodes contribute attacker-controlled XPointer selector text and URI state to `ctxt->incTab`. For a local-document include, `xmlXIncludeLoadDoc()` recognizes the include as local when the resolved `URL` is empty, starts with `#`, or equals `ctxt->doc->URL`, sets `doc = NULL`, evaluates the selector against `ctxt->doc`, and caches the resulting `xmlXPathObjectPtr` in `ctxt->incTab[nr]->xptr` instead of copying the selected nodes immediately. Phase 3 then walks the same include table in document order and calls `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()` for entries whose `inc`, `xptr`, or `emptyFb` is set. Because `ctxt->parseFlags` still carries `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE`, that phase uses the branch that unlinks and frees include nodes with `xmlFreeNode(cur)` after splicing in replacement content. The saved AddressSanitizer report shows that, for this witness, one of those phase-3 frees at `xinclude.c:2277` occurs before a later deferred local-document copy dereferences `ctxt->incTab[nr]->xptr` in `xmlXIncludeCopyXPointer()` at `xinclude.c:1162`. The staged malformed input proves the deferred-alias mechanism and the recorded free/read linkage, but it does not by source inspection alone identify the exact selected node inside the cached node set. The fix removes the deferred `xptr` cache for local-document includes, resolves the local-document path with `doc = ctxt->doc`, copies the XPointer result immediately, and no longer leaves a cached node set alive across later phase-3 substitutions.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that consumes the fuzz target's main-entity bytes and materializes parser state for the XML document whose XInclude nodes later populate `ctxt->incTab`.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` is in libxml2 fuzz format: after the 4-byte options word and string delimiters, the first entity string becomes the main document body later parsed by `xmlReadMemory()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is the first project statement on the vulnerable path that materializes the attacker-controlled XPointer selector from a `<xi:include>` element and stores it into the include-table entry later resolved into a stale `xmlXPathObjectPtr`.

root_cause.description: For local-document XIncludes, the vulnerable code retains the evaluated XPointer object in the include table instead of copying the selected nodes immediately. That keeps `xptr->nodesetval->nodeTab[]` alive across later phase-3 substitutions even though the same phase can free original document nodes before the deferred copy runs.
root_cause.note: The patch removes `xptr` from `xmlXIncludeRef`, replaces `doc = NULL` with `doc = ctxt->doc` for local-document includes, and always copies the XPointer result immediately before freeing the `xmlXPathObjectPtr`, eliminating the deferred alias that ASan later shows dangling for this witness.

sink.description: ASan sink. While copying a deferred local-document XPointer result, the function reads the `type` field of a node pointer still stored in the cached node set after that node has already been freed by an earlier include replacement.
sink.note: Stage 01's symbolized crash trace reports `READ of size 4` at `xinclude.c:1162` in `xmlXIncludeCopyXPointer`, and the freed-by stack points back to `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` line 2277.

parser_admitted.description: The parsed main document contains at least one element in the XInclude namespace whose structure passes `xmlXIncludeTestNode()`, so XInclude processing enters the include-collection path instead of treating the parsed tree as ordinary XML only.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz envelope supplies both the parser option word and the main entity bytes; the option word enables XInclude processing, and the main entity is parsed into a document tree.
XInclude phase 1 walks the parsed document, recognizes include elements, stores their URI/XPointer state in `ctxt->incTab`, and preserves the attacker-controlled parse flags in the XInclude context.

During phase 2, a local-document include is identified by the resolved `URL`, its XPointer is evaluated against `ctxt->doc`, and the resulting `xmlXPathObjectPtr` is cached in `ctxt->incTab[nr]->xptr` instead of being copied immediately.

Phase 3 iterates over the same include table; because `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` is set, it frees include nodes after replacement while deferred local-document `xptr` objects can still remain cached for later entries.

When a later cached local-document entry is expanded, the deferred XPointer copy dereferences a node pointer that the saved ASan report shows was already freed earlier in phase 3, producing the recorded heap-use-after-free read.

fine_trace.note: The staged fuzz envelope's first four bytes are materialized as the parser option word. For this witness they decode to `0x2020ffff`, which includes both `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` and `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE`.
The remaining fuzz payload is decoded into the main entity string and its URL. Those bytes are the XML body later parsed into the document that XInclude processing mutates.
Source. The fuzz target's main-entity bytes are converted into a parser context that will build the document tree later traversed by XInclude processing.
Because the attacker-controlled option word carries `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE`, the parsed document is sent into XInclude processing with the same flags that were read from the fuzz envelope.
The XInclude context stores the attacker-controlled parser flags. The later replacement logic tests this field to decide whether include markers are preserved or freed.

For an accepted `<xi:include>` node, phase 1 reads the attacker-controlled `xpointer` attribute text from the parsed element. That selector is the basis of the later XPath object cached in the include table.

The include's `href` is normalized into the `URL` string that will be stored in `ctxt->incTab[nr]->URI`. This URI value later decides whether `xmlXIncludeLoadDoc()` treats the include as local to the current document.

This include is handled as a local-document reference, so loading stays on `ctxt->doc` instead of parsing a separate document. The vulnerable deferred-XPointer path only uses `ctxt->incTab[nr]->xptr` when this local branch leaves `doc == NULL`.
Phase 2 evaluates the stored selector against `ctxt->doc` for this local include, producing an `xmlXPathObjectPtr` whose node set aliases nodes in the still-live original document.

depends_on.via: doc == NULL selects the local-document XPointer path

fine_trace.note: Root cause. Because this include is local, the evaluated XPath object is cached in `ctxt->incTab[nr]` instead of being copied immediately. The include table now retains node pointers into `ctxt->doc` across later substitutions.

fine_trace.code:
if ((ctxt->incTab[i]->inc != NULL) ||
            (ctxt->incTab[i]->xptr != NULL) ||
	    (ctxt->incTab[i]->emptyFb != 0))	/* (empty fallback) */
	    xmlXIncludeIncludeNode(ctxt, i);
fine_trace.note: Phase 3 iterates the include table in collection order. Entries with `inc`, cached `xptr`, or `emptyFb` are dispatched through `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()`, so a local-document `xptr` cached in step 10 can survive until a later loop iteration instead of being copied during phase 2.

The attacker-controlled `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` bit selects the branch that removes each original include marker after splicing in the replacement list. The saved free site at line 2277 is only reachable through this predicate.

This branch unlinks and frees the current include node. Stage 01's ASan trace names this exact statement as the free site that precedes the later read at `xinclude.c:1162`, although the malformed staged witness does not statically expose which cached selected node overlapped that freed allocation.

When phase 3 later reaches a local entry whose `inc` is still `NULL` and whose cached `xptr` is still present, it defers the copy until this call site and passes that cached XPath object into `xmlXIncludeCopyXPointer()`. This is the late-reload point enabled by the root cause in step 10.

Sink. The deferred copy walks `obj->nodesetval` and reads `set->nodeTab[i]->type`. AddressSanitizer reports `READ of size 4` here and links the accessed region back to the earlier `xmlFreeNode(cur)` at line 2277, establishing the witness's free-before-read even though the exact selected node identity is not recoverable from the staged malformed input alone.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The root cause is not the allocation site; it is the deferred ownership of an XPath object whose node set aliases nodes later freed by another include replacement.

poc.trigger: Run the staged `poc` through the libxml2 XML/XInclude parser with XInclude processing enabled so phase 3 expands multiple local-document `<xi:include>` entries; one earlier replacement frees nodes still referenced by a later cached XPointer result, and the later deferred copy crashes in `xmlXIncludeCopyXPointer`.

format.name: libxml2 fuzz xml target envelope
format.contract: The saved witness must decode as a libxml2 fuzz-XML input whose option word enables XInclude processing and `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE`, and whose main entity parses into a document accepted by `xmlXIncludeDoProcess()` with multiple local-document XInclude/XPointer references processed in document order. The required witness property is that one earlier phase-3 replacement can free original document nodes still referenced by a later deferred local-document XPointer cached in `ctxt->incTab[nr]->xptr`. The deleted regression file in the patch is supporting source evidence for that bug pattern, not the asserted byte-level shape of this specific staged `poc`.
